head.h1: Chinese New Year Catering in Dubai — Menus, Prices and What's Included

opening_paragraph: Chinese New Year catering in Dubai from myCHEF costs from AED 700 per person for a full reunion-dinner banquet. A vetted chef plans the auspicious pan-Asian menu, cooks it on site, serves your table and clears away. The spring festival is about the reunion dinner — a table crowded with dishes chosen for luck and abundance, shared by every guest at once. MyCHEF brings that feast to your home, villa, office or venue, tailored to your guest count and taste. Send your date, numbers and location, and promptly during our published business hours you'll have an itemised proposal to review.

new_paragraphs: How much does chinese new year catering cost in Dubai?
It starts from around AED 700 per person and is quoted by guest count, menu and service level. Set packages run from about AED 1200; send your numbers for an itemised quote.
What's included in a Chinese New Year catering package?
Included is menu design, a vetted chef cooking on site, service staff where needed, plating, setup and full cleanup — plus equipment and allergen labelling on request.
Do you cater halal Chinese New Year menus in Dubai?
Yes — every dish can be built fully halal. We confirm halal sourcing, note allergens and accommodate any dietary needs before finalising the menu.
Can you cater a corporate Chinese New Year event?
Yes. Corporate bookings range from office lunches and client dinners to gala banquets, with finger food, live stations or a plated multi-course menu, staff and setup all included.
Do you offer vegetarian and vegan Chinese New Year dishes?
Yes. Vegetable dumplings, tofu and mushroom stir-fries, longevity noodles and vegan spring rolls sit alongside the meat and seafood courses on request.
When is Chinese New Year, and how does that affect booking?

Chinese New Year 2026 fell on 17 February, the Year of the Horse, and the next is 6 February 2027, the Year of the Goat. The date moves with the lunar calendar and the celebration runs about a fortnight, so demand concentrates across that whole window and not just the one night.
How far ahead should I book Chinese New Year catering?

Allow about 72 hours for a standard package, 3 to 5 days for live stations, and 5 to 7 days for a bespoke banquet or a large party; 7 to 14 days or more for a corporate gala. Book further ahead again for dates inside the festival fortnight.
For chinese new year catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .

add_block.new_heading: Chinese New Year menu and food options
new_paragraphs: The menu is built around the dishes that carry meaning, then tailored entirely to your table. A classic chinese new year menu opens with dumplings and dim sum (wealth), moves through a whole steamed fish (surplus and togetherness), spring rolls (gold bars), longevity noodles and a glossy braise, and closes with nian gao or tang yuan for sweetness and unity. Beyond the symbolic staples, our chinese new year food catering spans Cantonese roasts, Sichuan heat, hand-pulled noodles, Peking duck carved tableside and a dessert cart of sesame balls and mango pudding. Every menu is fully customisable: all-halal on request, vegetarian and vegan courses (vegetable dumplings, tofu and mushroom stir-fries, vegan spring rolls), nut-free, and mindful of any allergy at your table. These are starting points — your final chinese new year menu in Dubai is designed with you, not off a fixed list.

add_block.new_heading: Symbolism and styling: setting a lucky table
new_paragraphs: Good Chinese New Year catering is as much about how the table reads as how it tastes, and the small touches matter. Partners plate for colour and abundance — red and gold, dishes served whole, nothing cut in a way that "cuts" the luck. The fish arrives head-on and pointed toward the guest of honour; oranges and tangerines cluster as edible décor for prosperity; dumplings are folded into ingot shapes. On request we coordinate red-and-gold linens, lanterns, a live noodle-pulling or dumpling station as entertainment, and a tea service to welcome elders first. Timing is planned around the reunion moment so the centrepiece lands when every guest is seated. If you're pairing the food with a lion dance or fireworks view, we build the courses around the schedule so nothing sits waiting. It's the styling that turns a good meal into the festival.

add_block.new_heading: Chinese New Year in Dubai: dates, what's on, and hosting at home
new_paragraphs: Chinese New Year 2026 fell on 17 February and opened the Year of the Horse; the next falls on 6 February 2027, the Year of the Goat. The date moves because the festival follows the lunar calendar, and the celebration runs for roughly a fortnight after it. That is why most families in Dubai hold the reunion dinner on the nearest weekend rather than on the day itself, and why catering diaries fill across the whole two-week window instead of a single night.

Public activities around the date cluster in the malls, along the waterfront and at Global Village, which is still in season through February — lion dances, red-and-gold decoration and, in some years, fireworks. Line-ups are published a few weeks ahead and change from year to year, so check the venue's own listing for the date you are planning around. MyCHEF does not run those events; what we do is the meal, and we time the courses so the table is fed properly before anyone heads out to watch.

If you are weighing a Chinese restaurant in Dubai against hosting, the difference is control. A restaurant on the night of the festival means a fixed set menu, a fixed sitting and a room shared with everyone else's celebration. At home you get the lazy-Susan table, the dishes your family actually asks for, elders served first, and no clock on the evening. The trade is the work, and that is the part we take: the chef cooks in your kitchen, serves the table and leaves it clean. Where the budget is tighter, the same menu can arrive as a drop-off spread without service staff. Judge the options on one thing: the best chinese new year catering is whichever plan gets the whole fish and the longevity noodles to the table while every guest is sitting at it.
